title: Grouped data
examples: How do I find the estimated mean from a frequency table?
What is the modal class when data is grouped?
Can you show me how to find the median class step by step?

explain.say: Today we will look at grouped data sets. These sets put data into ranges. We can estimate measures like the mean. This helps us find a central value.
To estimate the mean, we use the class mark. The class mark is the middle value of a class. You find it by adding the limits and dividing by two.
Next, we multiply the class mark by the frequency. This gives us the total value for that class. We do this for every class in the table.

items: Find the middle value of a class
draw.label: Calculating the Class Mark

explain.say: Finally, to get the estimated mean, we sum up all the values from the last column. Then, we divide this total by the total number of students. This gives our best estimate.

items: Calculate total value for each class

draw.text: Estimated Mean = Sum(f x x) / Total Frequency

faq.q: What is the class mark again?
faq.a: The class mark is simply the middle point of a data range. You find it by adding the lower and upper limits together and then dividing by two. You can also find it by averaging the two boundaries.
asks: How do I find the middle value of a class?
What is the midpoint of a class interval?

faq.q: Do I need to use the actual data points?
faq.a: No, because the data is grouped, we use the class mark instead. The class mark represents all the values within that specific class range. It is an estimate.
asks: Can I use the actual numbers if I know them?
Why do we use the class mark instead of the numbers?

faq.q: How do I find the estimated mean from a table?
faq.a: First, find the class mark for each row. Then multiply the frequency by that class mark. Finally, sum these products and divide by the total frequency. Follow these steps carefully.
asks: What is the process for estimating the mean?
Show me the steps for grouped data mean.

faq.q: Is the estimated mean always close to the real mean?
faq.a: Yes, the estimated mean is designed to be a good approximation. It gives us a reliable central value when we do not have every single data point. It is an estimate, not the exact value.

faq.q: What is the difference between the mean and the class mark?
faq.a: The mean is the calculated average of all data points. The class mark is just a representative number for a whole group or class. We use the class mark as a stand-in for the mean calculation.
asks: Why do we substitute the class mark?

facts: The class mark is calculated by averaging the class boundaries.
The estimated mean uses the class mark as a representative value.
The formula for the estimated mean is Sum(f x x) divided by Sum(f).
Frequency shows how many times a value or range appears.

quiz.say: A class has a lower limit of 10 and an upper limit of 20. What is the class mark?
quiz.why: You add the lower limit and the upper limit, then divide by two to find the exact middle point.

wrong.0: This is only the upper limit, not the middle of the range.
wrong.1: This is the sum of the limits, forgetting to divide by two.
wrong.3: This is only the lower limit, not the middle of the range.

quiz.say: If a class has a class mark of 25 and a frequency of 4, what is the product?
quiz.why: You multiply the frequency, which is four, by the class mark, which is twenty-five.

wrong.0: This incorrectly divides the product by the frequency.
wrong.2: This incorrectly adds the frequency and the class mark together.
wrong.3: This incorrectly divides the frequency by the class mark.

quiz.say: To find the estimated mean, what must you do with the final sum?

options.show: Add the total sum to the class mark
options.say: Add the total sum to the class mark

options.show: Take the square root of the total sum
options.say: Take the square root of the total sum

options.show: Divide the total sum by the total frequency
options.say: Divide the total sum by the total frequency

quiz.why: The final step is always to divide the total calculated sum by the total number of items counted.

wrong.0: Squaring the sum is not part of the standard mean calculation process.
wrong.1: You must divide the sum, not add the class mark to it.
wrong.2: Taking the square root is not the correct mathematical operation here.
